result.reason: Both items are a continuous Gemara exchange — Rabba's objection from the Nedarim mishna and its refutation — directly discussing the permitted indirect method of hinting to a storekeeper, which is precisely the content the 'Nedarim Mishnah' prose section describes.

All three items cover the core Mishnah scenarios about helping someone under a vow — the storekeeper/workers arrangement, the traveling companion/hefker case, and Rabbi Yose's objection with the Beit Horon reference — which Candidate 0's prose explicitly discusses as a unified block of 'Provision Scenarios.'

The passage directly discusses Rabbi Yehuda's distinction between Israelite and kohen, Abaye's resolution that the chiddush is the kohen's wife rule, and Rava's distinction between a full thirty-day month and a deficient month — exactly what the 'Yehudah Distinctions' prose describes.

The passage contains both Rav's and Shmuel's positions stated together, but the prose under 'Rav Position' (index 0) explicitly introduces this as 'the core dispute between Rav and Shmuel' and describes exactly the content of this Talmudic quote — the mefaresh/stam distinction and Shmuel's response — making it the passage that introduces and presents the combined dispute, whereas index 1 only elaborates on Shmuel's position in isolation.

Both items together form the classic Gemara objection ('haven't they already disputed this?') and its tzricha resolution explaining why the dispute must be stated in both the tashmish and mezonot contexts — exactly what the 'Articulation Logic' prose describes.

Both items present the Gemara's question against Shmuel (item 1) and its resolution by rereading the Mishnah as a case where she vowed and he affirmed it (item 2), which is precisely the content described in candidate 7 ('Shmuel Problem') — the problem Shmuel faces and the need to explain the difference — rather than candidate 8, which already describes the solution in its own prose and would be redundant with item 2.

All five items constitute the Gemara's successive attempts to rearrange the names in the baraita to reconcile contradictions — the 'reverse the attributions,' 'mix the pairs,' and final 'stam de-lo ke-Rabbi Meir' resolutions — which is exactly what the 'Name Reconciliation' prose describes.

Both items together present the Gemara's challenge from the Nedarim Mishnah about Rabbi Yossi's innuy nefesh threshold — item 1 raises the contradiction and item 2 gives the resolution ('bidvarim she-beino l'veinah') — which is precisely what the 'Innuy Nefesh Threshold' prose describes as the Gemara's challenge regarding which vow category applies to Rabbi Yossi's position.

The passage directly presents the Rav Huna/Rav Adda bar Ahava dispute about whether the husband can annul beino l'veinah vows, including the fox-in-the-burrow analogy, which is precisely what the prose of candidate 1 ('Beino L'Veinah Annul') describes and analyzes.

All three items — the pivot to the contingency-vow reading, Rav Kahana's ruling cited in support, and the 'karu lah menuveles' answer — are precisely what candidate 1 ('Vow Structure') describes as the Gemara's new and final reading of the Mishnah, including the adornment-as-condition structure and the social-embarrassment resolution.

The passage directly answers why there is no waiting period (the question posed in candidate 0's prose), and candidate 1's prose already paraphrases/explains this same Gemara text, meaning the Talmudic source belongs under the heading that poses the question it answers — candidate 0, 'Calm Affirmation.'

The passage directly presents the three amoraic opinions on what constitutes a 'stated limit' — twelve months, ten years, and until the next festival — which is precisely what the 'Time Standards' section prose describes.
